Abstract / methods: Operating rooms, our clusters, were each randomized in each 4-week blocks to either active or identical-looking sham supplemental air sterilization. All investigators, clinicians, and patients were fully blinded to treatment. No other aspect of anesthetic or surgical management was proscribed. Intent-to-treat analysis was restricted to adults who had surgery lasting at least an hour without evidence of pre-existing wound infections. We tested the primary hypothesis that supplemental active purification reduces a collapsed (one or more) composite of surgical wound infections, infection-related complications, or death within 30 days after inpatient surgery. Secondarily, we tested the hypothesis that supplemental air purification reduces the same composite after combined inpatient and outpatient surgeries.
Abstract / background: Surgical infections are the most common nosocomial infections and cause substantial morbidity and mortality. Operating rooms are relatively clean, but far from sterile. An unknown fraction of infections result from wound contamination by air-borne bacteria. We therefore tested the hypothesis that supplemental air purification reduces wound infections and related complications.

clinical_summary.text: In critically ill adults in the ICU who met criteria for weaning from high-flow nasal cannula (HFNC), three different weaning strategies—flow reduction first, FiO2 reduction first, or simultaneous reduction—were compared. The authors found no statistically significant differences among the groups in HFNC weaning success rates or duration. This suggests that any of these weaning approaches may be reasonable, as none showed clear superiority in this population.
clinical_summary.result_quote: The weaning success rates in the FR, OR, and SR groups were 94%, 81%, and 77%, respectively (p = 0.15). The median [interquartile range] weaning duration was 31.0 hours (29.0-45.8 hr), 29.5 hours (28.0-60.4 hr), and 29.5 hours (26.5-45.0 hr) in the FR, OR, and SR groups, respectively, with no statistically significant difference among groups (p = 0.87).

pubmed_facts.design: This multicenter, randomized controlled trial was conducted from December 1, 2022, to August 31, 2024, based on the suggested protocol (SLOWH trial). Experts reviewed the trial between October 2, 2024, and April 15, 2025.
pubmed_facts.population: Adults (≥ 18 yr old) in the ICU who met the weaning criteria after receiving HFNC were included. Among 102 patients from three tertiary care hospitals, 15 were excluded. Randomization was performed by a research coordinator using a sequence of random numbers generated by an independent statistician blinded to both researchers and participants.
pubmed_facts.intervention_comparator: The remaining patients were randomized into three intervention groups: flow reduction (FR) first, Fio2 reduction (OR) first, or simultaneous reduction (SR). The primary outcome was the HFNC weaning success rate, defined as successful transition to conventional oxygen therapy without the need for HFNC reapplication, noninvasive ventilation, or endotracheal intubation within 24 hours.

pubmed.population_setting: This prospective, randomized trial enrolled 211 healthy volunteers. Participants were randomized to one of five anesthetic regimens: sevoflurane, sevoflurane with remifentanil, sevoflurane with fentanyl, desflurane, or isoflurane. The primary outcome measure was the BIS50 for each anesthetic regimen, representing the BIS index at which 50% of participants were unresponsive. Secondary outcomes included BIS95 (representing the BIS index at which 95% of participants were unresponsive) and evaluation of the BIS index as a predictor of responsiveness. One hundred and forty-three participants were randomized to a treatment group and completed the procedure with adequate data.

The primary outcome measure was the BIS50 for each anesthetic regimen, representing the BIS index at which 50% of participants were unresponsive. Secondary outcomes included BIS95 (representing the BIS index at which 95% of participants were unresponsive) and evaluation of the BIS index as a predictor of responsiveness. One hundred and forty-three participants were randomized to a treatment group and completed the procedure with adequate data.
pubmed_facts.intervention_comparator: Opioids were administered by target-controlled infusion and commenced before the inhaled agent began.
pubmed_facts.primary_endpoint: The primary outcome measure was the BIS50 for each anesthetic regimen, representing the BIS index at which 50% of participants were unresponsive.
pubmed_facts.reported_results: One hundred and forty-three participants were randomized to a treatment group and completed the procedure with adequate data. Mean age was 26.5 ± 6.7 years (52% male). There were no reported device-related adverse events. Across treatment groups, BIS50 ranged from 67.5 (95% confidence interval [CI], 63.6-71.4) to 76.2 (73.5-78.8), and BIS95 ranged from 49.1 (42.9-55.4) to 63.3 (59.5-67.2). Compared to the sevoflurane and isoflurane groups, the desflurane group exhibited slightly lower BIS50 and BIS95 values. The addition of opioids to sevoflurane had minimal impact on BIS50 and BIS95. The BIS index alone was a strong predictor of the level of responsiveness, with AUCs consistently close to the ideal value of 1 (≥0.95) across all treatment groups. BIS indices were highly correlated with MOAA/S scores.
pubmed_facts.conclusions: These results describe the relationship between BIS levels and responsiveness for commonly used volatile anesthetics, with and without opioids, across a range of anesthetic concentrations. The results of this study should be interpreted in light of the study design which included young, healthy adult volunteers with no sustained, noxious stimulation. These findings may not be generalizable to other populations or clinical situations.

Meaning : In healthy volunteers receiving various inhaled anesthetic agents with or without opioids, BIS index was highly correlated with Modified Observer’s Assessment of Alertness/Sedation (MOAA/S) scores and was a strong predictor of the level of responsiveness. In recent decades, the anesthesia research community has made significant advances in the understanding and interpretation of intraoperative electroencephalogram (EEG) signals. These advances have led to the widespread adoption of processed EEG (pEEG) technologies in modern anesthesia practice for certain applications. Anesthesiologists commonly use intraoperative pEEG monitoring as part of routine care, personalizing the anesthetic by titrating the drug dosage to the EEG signal in an effort to avoid both under- and overdosing. 1 The Bispectral Index TM Brain Monitoring System (BIS TM ) processes raw EEG signals to monitor the level of hypnosis and anesthesia. 2–8 It helps guide effective titration of anesthetics and has been shown to be associated with more favorable recovery outcomes, 9 , 10 though other reports have shown limited utility in practice. 11 As a mature technology with a voluminous literature, the limitations of BIS are also well known and include some vulnerability with artifactual disturbances such as the electromyogram, 12 issues relating to the presence of certain drugs such as nitrous oxide and ketamine, 13 , 14 and concerns relating to the opioid-hypnotic ratio. 15 Common agents used for maintenance of anesthesia are halogenated inhaled agents such as sevoflurane, isoflurane, desflurane, and intravenous agents such as propofol. 16 The BIS patterns and recovery time differ depending on the anesthetic used. 17 Previous reports have explored changes to BIS indices under a variety of anesthesia regimens, though for any individual study the regimen is usually limited to a single sedative and opioid. Part of the knowledge gap addressed by the study is to describe the concentration–effect relationship for all these agents in a single study using the same methods. The primary aim of this study was to determine the BIS index at which 50% of participants were unresponsive (BIS 50 ) for each anesthetic regimen. Assignments were not blinded.

Abstract / methods: A scoping review was conducted in accordance with Joanna Briggs Institute methodology and reported as per Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses Extension for Scoping Reviews. A protocol was registered on the Open Science Framework. MEDLINE, MEDLINE ePubs and In-Process Citations, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, and Cochrane databases were searched. Eligible studies included adult or paediatric surgical patients undergoing perioperative diaphragmatic ultrasound. Data were charted on study characteristics, ultrasound techniques, reference standards, and measures of diagnostic accuracy and inter- and intra-observer agreement.
Abstract / background: Diaphragmatic dysfunction contributes to perioperative respiratory morbidity. Point-of-care ultrasound enables noninvasive bedside assessment of diaphragmatic structure and motion and is increasingly used in perioperative practice. However, its diagnostic performance and measurement reliability in this setting have not been systematically evaluated. This scoping review aimed to map the available evidence, with emphasis on reliability, reproducibility, and agreement with reference standards.

pubmed_facts.design: This prospective, population-based cohort study included adults (≥18 years) who received EMS-attempted resuscitation and survived to hospital discharge following non-traumatic OHCA in Victoria, Australia, between July 2019 and June 2022.
pubmed_facts.primary_endpoint: Primary outcomes were fatigue (Modified Fatigue Impact Scale), anxiety and depression (Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale).
pubmed_facts.reported_results: Of 1068 eligible 12-month survivors, 728 (68.2%) completed follow-up (median age 61 years; 555 [76.2%] male). Fatigue was reported by 35.8% (250/699), anxiety by 22.6% (162/716), and depression by 18.0% (129/716). Higher symptom burden was associated with lower EQ-5D and SF-12 scores, worse GOSE outcomes (all p<0.001) and reduced return-to-work rates. Compared with population norms, survivors reported greater fatigue (SMD 0.64; 95%CI, 0.50-0.78;p<0.001), and depression (SMD, 0.12; 95%CI, 0.02,0.21;p=0.02) but lower anxiety (SMD, -0.27; 95%CI, -0.35 to -0.18;p<0.001). In adjusted models, younger age, preexisting anxiety or depression, diabetes and initial non-shockable arrest were associated with higher symptom burden, whereas EMS-witnessed arrests were associated with lower symptom burden.

Abstract / methods: This prospective, population-based cohort study included adults (≥18 years) who received EMS-attempted resuscitation and survived to hospital discharge following non-traumatic OHCA in Victoria, Australia, between July 2019 and June 2022. Survivors were identified from a statewide OHCA registry and completed a 12-month telephone interview. Primary outcomes were fatigue (Modified Fatigue Impact Scale), anxiety and depression (Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale). Secondary outcomes included HRQoL (EQ-5D, SF-12), functional recovery (GOSE), living arrangement, and return to work.
Abstract / objectives: To determine the prevalence and factors associated with fatigue, anxiety, and depression 12 months after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA); examine their associations with health-related quality of life (HRQoL) and functional recovery; and compare symptom burden with population norms.

pubmed_facts.reported_results: Among the 41,622,004 surgical admissions, people living with HIV were found to be older and carried a significantly higher comorbidity burden, with a Charlson Comorbidity Index of 8 compared to 1 in the HIV-negative group. Perioperative organ injury occurred in 1,348,363 of 2,088,307 people living with HIV (64.6%) compared with 7,867,547 of 39,533,697 HIV-negative patients (19.9%). Acute myocardial infarction (33.5%) and acute kidney injury (22.0%) were the most common injuries among people living with HIV. In-hospital mortality occurred in 66,935 of 2,088,307 people living with HIV (3.2%) compared with 872,170 of 39,533,697 HIV-negative patients (2.2%). Hospital length of stay and hospital charges were also significantly higher. Adjusted analyses demonstrated that HIV status was independently associated with higher in-hospital mortality (odds ratio [OR], 1.66; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.54-1.78), longer hospital length of stay (β = 2.73 days; 95% CI, 2.56-2.90), a decreased likelihood of home discharge (hazard ratio [HR], 0.73; 95% CI, 0.72-0.73), and increased hospitalization costs (β = $18,423; 95% CI, 16,712-20,134). Sensitivity analyses demonstrated that elevated perioperative risk persisted among patients with asymptomatic HIV infection, although the greatest risk was observed among patients with symptomatic HIV disease/AIDS.

Abstract / methods: This retrospective cohort study used data from the National Inpatient Sample (NIS) from 2016 to 2021. The population-based sample included adult patients (age >18 years) identified via International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision, Clinical Modification (ICD-10-CM) codes. Abstract / background: While antiretroviral therapy has improved surgical safety for people living with HIV, comprehensive data on perioperative organ injury and its impact on patient safety remain limited. This study aimed to compare the incidence of perioperative organ injury, in-hospital mortality, hospital length of stay, and hospitalization costs between people living with HIV and HIV-negative individuals undergoing surgery in the United States.

pubmed_facts.reported_results: Of 2,634 cardiac arrests, 958 met inclusion criteria, with 152 (15.9%) out-of-hospital arrests and 806 (84.1%) in-hospital. The mean initial post-arrest hemoglobin was 9.75 g/dL (SD 2.60), with hemoglobin levels declining progressively over the first 20 days post-arrest. Red cell transfusions were delivered for 369 (38.5%) patients in the 30 days post-arrest, with 1,238 total transfusions. The mean pre-transfusion hemoglobin value was 6.96 g/dL (SD 1.06). Pre-transfusion hemoglobin levels were < 7 g/dL for 762 (61.6%) of transfusions, and ≥ 7 g/dL for 476 (38.4%) of transfusions. Over 30 days, the highest proportion of patients transfused was in the first 48 h. Patients with initial post-arrest hemoglobin ≥ 9 g/dL had lower in-hospital mortality (adjusted OR 0.62, 95% CI 0.46-0.84, p<0.01). In time-varying analysis, post-arrest hemoglobin through 30 days demonstrated an L-shaped association with mortality, with 95% of the total reduction in mortality hazard captured below 9.20 g/dL.

Abstract / methods: We performed a retrospective cohort study of consecutive adult cardiac arrests at three academic hospitals. We screened in-hospital and out-of-hospital arrests with resuscitation efforts ongoing at hospital arrival for inclusion. Patients who survived the initial resuscitation and had a hemoglobin value measured were included. All post-arrest hemoglobin values and red blood cell transfusions were collected through 30 days; descriptive statistics and graphical visualization were used to present hemoglobin trends and transfusion practices. Exploratory analyses evaluated the association between hemoglobin and in-hospital mortality.
Abstract / background: Hemoglobin targets are absent from post-cardiac arrest guidelines. New trials suggest that patients with brain and myocardial injury, injuries common post-arrest, may benefit from higher hemoglobin targets. Trends in post-arrest hemoglobin and real-world practices remain poorly characterized.

pubmed_facts.reported_results: LMD was calculated over 3, 6, 12, and 24 hours (LMD3h-LMD24h). pubmed_facts.evidence: Abstract / unstructured: This study compared bag-valve-mask ventilation quality and adherence to the guideline-recommended ventilation volume range during 30:2 cardiopulmonary resuscitation for out-of-hospital cardiac arrest before and after the implementation of real-time feedback. We conducted a before-and-after observational study of two sequential adult cohorts with out-of-hospital cardiac arrest managed by basic life support teams from the Paris Fire Brigade. A bidirectional sensor measured insufflated volume (Vi) and expiratory tidal volume (Vt). The display was masked during Period-1 and provided real-time feedback during Period-2. We assessed adherence to the guideline-recommended range using mixed-effects regression; we analyzed Vt and leak volume using gamma log-link generalized linear mixed models. We analyzed 4,300 ventilations in 163 patients, 96 without feedback and 67 with feedback. Median Vi was lower with feedback (471 mL) than without (513 mL, p=0.03 for the first ventilation of each cycle) but median Vt was unchanged (235 vs. 243 mL, p=0.84). Vi dispersion was reduced by 35% (mean within-patient IQR ratio 0.65 [95%-CI, 0.53-0.77]). Vi was 400-600 mL in 68% of ventilations with feedback vs. 42% without feedback. In contrast, Vt was 400-600 mL in only 14% of ventilations with feedback vs. 15% without feedback. In multivariable analysis, leak volume was 12% lower with feedback (mean ratio, 0.88 [95%-CI, 0.77-0.99]). Real-time feedback was associated with improved adherence to the guideline-recommended range for Vi, less dispersed Vi,and lower leak volume. Causal inference, clinical significance, and generalizability warrant further evaluation.

pubmed.population_setting: "PRactice of VENTilation in critically ill patients without ARDS" (PRoVENT), "PRactice of VENTilation in critically ill patients in Middle-income Countries" (PRoVENT-iMiC), and "Extubation strategies in Neuro-ICU patients and associations with Outcomes" (ENIO). We excluded patients with ARDS at the start of ventilation. DATA EXTRACTION: Demographic and clinical characteristics, ventilator settings, respiratory variables, arterial blood gas values, and clinical outcomes were extracted from the harmonized PRIME database. Derived ventilation parameters included tidal volume normalized to predicted body weight, driving pressure, respiratory system compliance, mechanical power, ventilatory ratio, and Pao2/Fio2 ratio. DATA SYNTHESIS: This analysis included 3848 patients, including 1702 neurocritical care and 1920 non-neurocritical care patients. Based on recorded ventilatory variables, neurocritical care patients received lower median tidal volumes (Vts), positive end-expiratory pressure, and Fio2. They had lower median driving pressure (ΔP), mechanical power (MP) of ventilation, and ventilatory ratio, as well as higher respiratory system compliance compared with non-neurocritical care patients. These differences were consistently observed at both assessed time points. ARDS was diagnosed more frequently in neurocritical care patients than in non-neurocritical care patients (8.7% vs. 3.9%; p < 0.001), while ICU mortality was lower (14.3% vs. 22.8%; p < 0.001).

clinical_summary.text: In adults with severe ARDS who were successfully decannulated from V-V ECMO, permissive weaning (decannulation despite persistent abnormal respiratory mechanics) was associated with higher 90-day mortality compared to conventional weaning, according to retrospective single-center data. However, permissive weaning did not appear to delay liberation from mechanical ventilation by day 90. These findings suggest caution with permissive weaning strategies, though residual confounding cannot be excluded in this observational study.
clinical_summary.result_quote: In landmark analysis, permissive weaning was associated with higher 90-day mortality in both univariable (hazard ratio [HR] 3.53, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.62-7.66; p < 0.01) and multivariable analyses (adjusted HR 4.45, 95% CI 1.98-9.97; p < 0.01).

pubmed_facts.design: We conducted a retrospective single-center cohort study including adult patients with refractory ARDS treated with V-V ECMO between January 2015 and December 2022 who were successfully decannulated while receiving invasive mechanical ventilation. Permissive weaning was defined as ECMO decannulation despite persistence of at least one of the following criteria during the sweep gas-off trial: plateau pressure ≥30 cmH₂O, driving pressure ≥20 cmH₂O, positive end-expiratory pressure ≥15 cmH₂O, or tidal volume ≤5 mL/kg predicted body weight.

pubmed_facts.reported_results: Among 469 patients treated with V-V ECMO, 280 successfully decannulated patients were included; 117 (42%) underwent permissive weaning and 163 (58%) conventional weaning. Baseline characteristics were broadly similar, although body mass index was higher and SARS-CoV-2 ARDS more frequent in the permissive group. Some patients are decannulated despite persistent abnormalities in respiratory mechanics once oxygenation and carbon dioxide clearance are considered adequate. We aimed to compare outcomes associated with permissive versus conventional V-V ECMO weaning.

MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Functional status and quality of life at 1 year assessed using the 12-item World Health Organization Disability Assessment Schedule (WHODAS 2.0). Secondary outcomes included institutionalisation and mortality.
pubmed_facts.reported_results: After excluding 81 deaths and 462 nonresponders, the 1-year telephone follow-up was completed for 1899 patients. Postoperative delirium within the first 48 h was independently associated with a 4.6-point higher WHODAS score at 1 year: adjusted mean difference = 4.60 [95% confidence interval (CI), 1.57 to 7.64, P = 0.003]. Delirium was also associated with increased institutionalisation and higher mortality: odds ratio (OR) 2.5 (95% CI, 1.07 to 5.84, P = 0.03), and (16.7 vs. 3.1%; P < 0.001), including 30-day, 60-day, and 365-day mortality (all P < 0.001), respectively.

pubmed_facts.evidence:
Abstract / conclusions: Open/flexible ICU family presence may reduce delirium and shorten the duration of IMV slightly, without increasing infections or ICU mortality, although the certainty of evidence is low and heterogeneity remains substantial.
Abstract / objectives: To critically evaluate the comparative effects of open or flexible family presence policies vs. restricted or traditional family presence policies on the occurrence of delirium and other major outcomes among adult patients admitted to ICUs. DATA SOURCES: We conducted a comprehensive electronic search of MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, CINAHL, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials from inception to November 21, 2025. STUDY SELECTION: We included randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing open or flexible vs. restricted ICU visiting policies in adult patients. DATA EXTRACTION: The primary outcome extracted was delirium occurrence. Secondary outcomes included the duration of invasive mechanical ventilation (IMV), ICU length of stay, hospital-acquired infections, and ICU mortality. DATA SYNTHESIS: Thirteen RCTs comprising 3861 patients were included. Random-effects models showed that compared with restricted policies, open/flexible family presence reduced delirium occurrence (risk ratio [RR], 0.48; 95% CI, 0.29-0.81; low certainty) and IMV duration (mean difference [MD], -0.36 d; 95% CI, -0.46 to -0.26 d; low certainty).

pubmed_facts.design: We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL) from inception to January 2025 for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing perioperative ketamine or esketamine with placebo or standard care. Subgroup, meta‑regression, and trial sequential analysis (TSA) were performed.
pubmed_facts.population: We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL) from inception to January 2025 for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing perioperative ketamine or esketamine with placebo or standard care. Twenty-five RCTs (3344 patients) were included (ketamine: 9; esketamine: 16). Dizziness risk increased (RR 1.45, 95% CI, 1.14-1.84, P = .002), while postoperative depressive symptoms decreased (RR 0.78, 95% CI, 0.63-0.96, P = .02; based on 2 studies, 493 patients).
pubmed_facts.intervention_comparator: We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL) from inception to January 2025 for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing perioperative ketamine or esketamine with placebo or standard care.
pubmed_facts.primary_endpoint: The primary outcome was POD incidence (risk ratio [RR]).
pubmed_facts.reported_results: Twenty-five RCTs (3344 patients) were included (ketamine: 9; esketamine: 16). Both agents reduced POD risk versus control (ketamine: RR 0.69, 95% CI, 0.49-0.98, P = .04; esketamine: RR 0.58, 95% CI, 0.36-0.95, P = .03). Benefit was more evident with high-dose regimens (single bolus: ketamine >0.5 mg/kg or esketamine >0.25 mg/kg; cumulative dose: ketamine >1.0 mg/kg or esketamine >0.5 mg/kg), bolus-plus-infusion, and in major surgery. The effect was observed when POD was assessed 2 to 7 days postoperatively, but not within 24 hours. TSA indicated that current evidence remains inconclusive due to insufficient information size. Dizziness risk increased (RR 1.45, 95% CI, 1.14-1.84, P = .002), while postoperative depressive symptoms decreased (RR 0.78, 95% CI, 0.63-0.96, P = .02; based on 2 studies, 493 patients).
pubmed_facts.conclusions: Perioperative ketamine and esketamine show a potential signal for POD reduction, particularly with optimized dosing in high‑risk patients. However, the evidence is currently inconclusive, and increased dizziness risk precludes routine recommendation. Large, multicenter RCTs are urgently needed.

clinical_summary.text: In this scoping review of nine observational studies on patients undergoing ECMO weaning, various blood processing strategies—including autologous blood reinfusion and direct discard—were compared. The authors found that autologous blood reinfusion appears feasible and is associated with improved surrogate hematological outcomes versus direct discard, but due to limited, low-quality, and heterogeneous evidence, no conclusions can be drawn regarding effects on major clinical outcomes. Further high-quality studies are needed to determine long-term efficacy and safety.
clinical_summary.result_quote: A total of 68 articles were retrieved, and 9 studies were finally included. The identified blood processing strategies were classified into four categories: blood cell salvage system (BCS) autologous reinfusion, pump-controlled blood reinfusion, modified CPD blood bag storage reinfusion, and direct discard.

Abstract / methods: This scoping review strictly followed the PRISMA‑ScR 2018 checklist and JBI methodology. We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science Core Collection, Cochrane Library, CNKI, and Wanfang from inception to March 28, 2026. Two reviewers independently screened literature, extracted data, and assessed quality. Descriptive synthesis and qualitative analysis were performed due to high heterogeneity and lack of randomized controlled trials (RCTs).
Abstract / background: Extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) has been widely used for life support in severe refractory cardiac and respiratory failure. During ECMO weaning, the circuit usually retains 500-800 mL of residual blood. Direct discarding leads to blood loss, increased anemia, and higher allogeneic transfusion requirements, while appropriate autologous blood reinfusion can reduce transfusion risks and medical costs. However, evidence on blood processing strategies during ECMO weaning remains scattered, and no unified clinical guidelines exist.

clinical_summary.text: In high-risk patients undergoing elective major abdominal surgery, individualized cardiac index-guided hemodynamic therapy targeting each patient's preoperative resting cardiac index did not significantly reduce the incidence of a composite outcome (acute kidney injury, acute myocardial injury, severe infectious complications, nonfatal cardiac arrest, or death within 7 days) compared with routine hemodynamic therapy. There were also no differences in the rates of the individual components of this composite outcome between groups.
clinical_summary.result_quote: Among high-risk patients undergoing elective major abdominal surgery, individualized cardiac index-guided hemodynamic therapy targeting the patient's preoperative resting cardiac index did not reduce the incidence of a composite outcome of acute kidney injury, acute myocardial injury, severe infectious complications, nonfatal cardiac arrest, or death within the first 7 postoperative days compared with routine hemodynamic therapy.

pubmed_facts.population: This multicenter, single-blind, superiority randomized clinical trial enrolled high-risk patients undergoing elective major abdominal surgery between October 8, 2023, and October 25, 2025, at 12 university medical centers in Austria, the Czech Republic, Denmark, Germany, and Spain. The date of last follow-up was January 15, 2026.
pubmed_facts.intervention_comparator: Patients were randomized to individualized cardiac index-guided hemodynamic therapy targeting the patient's preoperative resting cardiac index vs routine hemodynamic therapy (with blinded cardiac index monitoring).
pubmed_facts.primary_endpoint: The primary outcome was a composite of acute kidney injury, acute myocardial injury, severe infectious complications, nonfatal cardiac arrest, or death within the first 7 postoperative days. Secondary outcomes included the individual components of the primary outcome within the first 7 postoperative days.
pubmed_facts.reported_results:
Of the 1128 patients enrolled, 1111 were randomized and 1095 were included in the primary analysis (median age, 67 years [IQR, 59-74 years]; 49.4% were female). The primary outcome occurred in 243 of 549 patients (44.3%) in the individualized cardiac index-guided hemodynamic therapy group vs 256 of 546 patients (46.9%) in the routine hemodynamic therapy group (relative risk, 0.94 [95.1% CI, 0.83-1.08]; P = .38). There were no between-group differences for the incidence of the individual components of the primary outcome within the first 7 postoperative days.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Among high-risk patients undergoing elective major abdominal surgery, individualized cardiac index-guided hemodynamic therapy targeting the patient's preoperative resting cardiac index did not reduce the incidence of a composite outcome of acute kidney injury, acute myocardial injury, severe infectious complications, nonfatal cardiac arrest, or death within the first 7 postoperative days compared with routine hemodynamic therapy.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT05648279.

pubmed_facts.design: Serum samples obtained from ACCESS trial patients at baseline and 72 hours were profiled using the Olink Target 96 Inflammation panel. Patients were grouped by treatment arm and by achievement of the trial's composite primary endpoint.
pubmed_facts.population: Serum samples obtained from ACCESS trial patients at baseline and 72 hours were profiled using the Olink Target 96 Inflammation panel. Patients were grouped by treatment arm and by achievement of the trial's composite primary endpoint. After quality control, 70 proteins from 394 paired samples across 197 patients were analyzed to assess differential expression within and between groups over time, evaluate associations with clinical outcomes, and identify immune endotypes using unsupervised clustering. Among patients achieving the primary endpoint, IL6, CXCL9, CXCL10, and IFN-γ were suppressed only in clarithromycin-treated individuals. The identification of distinct inflammatory endotypes suggests biological heterogeneity in CAP and supports future investigation of endotype-guided approaches to identify patients most likely to benefit from immunomodulatory therapies.
pubmed_facts.intervention_comparator: After quality control, 70 proteins from 394 paired samples across 197 patients were analyzed to assess differential expression within and between groups over time, evaluate associations with clinical outcomes, and identify immune endotypes using unsupervised clustering.
pubmed_facts.primary_endpoint: Patients were grouped by treatment arm and by achievement of the trial's composite primary endpoint.
pubmed_facts.reported_results:
IL6 was selectively downregulated on day 4 in the clarithromycin arm, whereas IFN-γ, CXCL9, CXCL10, and SCF decreased over time across both treatment arms, consistent with resolution of inflammation. Among patients achieving the primary endpoint, IL6, CXCL9, CXCL10, and IFN-γ were suppressed only in clarithromycin-treated individuals. Clustering consistently identified two inflammatory endotypes with comparable SOFA, but distinct RSS scores. The endotype with lower RSS demonstrated higher IFN-γ and globally elevated inflammatory protein expression; in that endotype 90-day mortality was decreased with clarithromycin treatment.
INTERPRETATION: Clarithromycin exerts measurable immunomodulatory effects in CAP, characterized by attenuation of pro-inflammatory cytokines, particularly IL6. The identification of distinct inflammatory endotypes suggests biological heterogeneity in CAP and supports future investigation of endotype-guided approaches to identify patients most likely to benefit from immunomodulatory therapies.
CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT04724044, EudraCT 2020-004452-15.

deep_dives.key_results:

The authors found no significant difference in CSA-AKI incidence or secondary outcomes such as mortality and ICU stay. However, the analysis was limited by insufficient sample size to draw definitive conclusions.

Abstract / objectives: Noninvasive ventilation (NIV) is widely used in acute respiratory failure (ARF), yet the association between high tidal volume (Vt) and clinical outcomes remains incompletely defined. We evaluated the association between Vt and NIV failure overall and by ARF type, and its relationship with respiratory and clinical outcomes. DATA SOURCES: MEDLINE, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, Web of Science, and Latin American and Caribbean Health Science Literature (1976 to September 2025). STUDY SELECTION: Observational studies of adults with ARF treated with NIV reporting Vt or Vt normalized to predicted body weight (Vt/PBW) in NIV success and failure groups. DATA EXTRACTION: Three pairs of reviewers identified studies and extracted data independently. Random-effects meta-analysis was performed. Risk of bias and certainty of evidence were assessed using Risk of Bias In Nonrandomized Studies of Interventions and Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation. DATA SYNTHESIS: Eleven studies (1136 patients) were included. Certainty of evidence ranged from very low to moderate.

Abstract / objectives: To evaluate the diagnostic accuracy and therapeutic utility of the furosemide stress test (FST) for acute kidney injury (AKI) management in critically ill adults and children. DATA SOURCES: PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials were searched from inception to March 3, 2026. STUDY SELECTION: Studies evaluating the standardized FST protocol in critically ill adults or children with AKI were eligible. Outcomes included AKI stage 3 progression (Q1), kidney replacement therapy (KRT) initiation (Q2), short-term mortality (Q3), successful KRT liberation (Q4), and FST-guided vs. standard KRT initiation in randomized trials (Q5). DATA EXTRACTION: Two reviewers independently extracted data and assessed risk of bias using Quality Assessment of Diagnostic Accuracy Studies 2 and Risk of Bias 2. Certainty of evidence was assessed using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) framework. DATA SYNTHESIS: Twenty studies (n = 1979; 11 countries; 2013-2025) were included. For AKI progression (nine studies; n = 501), pooled sensitivity was 0.69 and specificity was 0.88 (area under the curve [AUC], 0.89; GRADE: low).

pubmed.title: Furosemide Stress Test in Adults and Children With Acute Kidney Injury: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

clinical_summary.text: In adults undergoing pancreaticoduodenectomy with positive intraoperative bile cultures, withholding pre-emptive antibiotics did not increase early postoperative complications or infections compared to those who received antibiotics, based on a multicenter propensity-matched cohort study. However, five-year mortality was higher in the no-antibiotic group only in the matched cohort, a finding the authors caution may reflect residual confounding rather than a causal effect. These results suggest early outcomes are similar, but long-term survival implications remain uncertain.
clinical_summary.result_quote: Five-year mortality was higher in the group without PE-ATB in the matched cohort (hazard ratio, 2.02; 95% confidence interval, 1.01-4.04; P = 0.048), whereas no survival difference was observed in the overall unmatched cohort.

Abstract / methods: This multicenter retrospective cohort study included 301 consecutive adults undergoing pancreaticoduodenectomy with positive intraoperative bile cultures in four French tertiary centers between January 2014 and December 2024. Overall, 89 patients received PE-ATB, and 212 did not. Propensity score matching at a 1:2 ratio yielded 138 patients, including 46 treated patients and 92 controls. Abstract / background: Pre-emptive antibiotic therapy is frequently prescribed after pancreaticoduodenectomy when intraoperative bile cultures are positive, despite the absence of clinical infection. Evidence supporting this practice remains limited. We assessed the association between withholding pre-emptive antibiotics and postoperative outcomes in patients with biliary colonization.

Abstract / background: Pre-emptive antibiotic therapy is frequently prescribed after pancreaticoduodenectomy when intraoperative bile cultures are positive, despite the absence of clinical infection. Abstract / conclusions: A systematic difference between cRCTs and iRCTs in length-of-stay- or days-alive-type outcomes, but not mortality, was identified, with cRCTs reporting smaller effect size magnitudes than iRCTs. With under half of identified meta-analyses reporting on randomization modality, these results highlight the need for improved transparency and statistical consideration of randomization type in future meta-analyses in prehospital, emergency, and critical care.
Abstract / objectives: Cluster-randomized clinical trials (cRCTs) are pooled with individually randomized clinical trials (iRCTs) in meta-analyses. However, cRCTs are associated with methodological characteristics potentially inducing systematic differences compared with iRCTs. In acute settings, trial inclusion is time-sensitive, exacerbating inclusion-based biases. We conducted a meta-epidemiological study to assess deviations in effect estimates between cRCTs and iRCTs in these settings. DATA SOURCES: A systematic literature search was conducted in PubMed and Embase. DATA SELECTION: We screened and identified all meta-analyses in prehospital, emergency, or critical care within the last decade that included at least one cRCT and one iRCT. DATA EXTRACTION: Data were extracted in duplicate from the meta-analyses. If overlapping trials were identified, results were pooled. The primary outcome was mortality; the secondary outcome comprised length-of-stay- or days-alive-type outcomes. We identified 94 eligible meta-analyses; 44.7% reported on randomization type (cRCT or iRCT).

pubmed_facts.reported_results: Consensus was achieved on 20 statements across three domains: (1) operational criteria to prompt endotoxemia assessment in suspected or presumed septic shock, (2) role and interpretation of the EAA, and (3) logistics and clinical implementation of PMX-HA. pubmed_facts.design:
Randomized controlled trial with two parallel groups: control group receiving standard care during weaning and MG receiving music therapy additionally.
SETTING AND
pubmed_facts.population: Adult critically ill patients (n = 100) admitted to a general ICU who received IMV for at least 48 hours.
pubmed_facts.intervention_comparator: MG received daily, individualized music therapy sessions averaging 25 minutes, based on patient needs and musical preferences, which included music relaxation, music listening, and clinical improvisation.
pubmed_facts.reported_results: No significant difference in weaning duration was observed between groups (p = 0.97). Patients in the MG group showed significant improvements in agitation and sedation levels (Richmond Agitation-Sedation Scale) on days 1 and 3 (p = 0.048, 0.005, and 0.024) and a lower percentage required propofol (p = 0.028). No significant difference in perceived pain (Visual Analog Pain Scale). The MG obtained lower Perceived Stress Scale-14 scores (p = 0.24). Additionally, MG significantly reduced tracheostomy rates (14%; p = 0.025). Median total IMV and ICU stay duration were shorter in the MG group, but not significantly (p = 0.206 and 0.203). Heart rate, respiratory rate, blood pressure, and oxygenation showed no significant difference before and after music therapy.

Articles were excluded based on the following criteria: (1) inclusion of pediatric populations or cardiac surgery performed without cardiopulmonary bypass; (2) failure to report measures related to the predictive performance of CSA-AKI; and (3) an inappropriate study design, including secondary studies (systematic reviews or meta-analyses), case reports, and case series. Titles and abstracts were manually screened by two independent reviewers (P.L.B. and J.B.H.). Discrepancies were resolved by consensus. When consensus could not be reached, a third reviewer (R.S.) made the final decision on inclusion. Data extraction and quality assessment Two reviewers independently performed data extraction and quality assessment, using a previously published template [ 17 ]. In cases of disagreement, discrepancies were resolved through discussion and consensus. The PROBAST results are illustrated in Supplementary Figures S1 and S2.

We included all RCTs of prehabilitation that included at least one exercise intervention (aerobic, strength, pulmonary, or functional exercises) and that reported at least one critical outcome (postoperative complications, length of stay, health-related quality of life, or physical recovery). P-scores were used to rank interventions by their probability of being most beneficial.
pubmed_facts.reported_results: We screened 7660 citations, reviewed 1480 full-text articles, and included 96 unique RCTs (N=7396). Combined aerobic, pulmonary, and functional exercise were most likely to reduce complications (P-score 0.94, odds ratio 0.16, 95% CI 0.05-0.60; very low certainty) and length of stay (P-score 0.97, mean difference -3.4 days, 95% CI -5.7 to -1.0; moderate certainty). Combined aerobic and strength exercise was most likely to improve health-related quality of life (P-score 0.93, standardised mean difference 0.67, 95% CI 0.07-1.27; low certainty). No exercise interventions significantly improved physical recovery.

Abstract / methods: In this single-centre, parallel-group RCT, adults with intermediate to high risk for PPCs (ARISCAT score ≥26) who underwent laparoscopic colorectal surgery were randomly assigned to receive intraoperative PEEP titration guided by EIT or a conventional fixed PEEP of 5 cm H2O. The primary outcome was PPCs incidence within 30 days, as determined by a multidisciplinary adjudication team using standardised criteria.
Abstract / background: Pneumoperitoneum and steep Trendelenburg positioning during laparoscopic colorectal surgery promote atelectasis and increase the risk of postoperative pulmonary complications (PPCs). Electrical impedance tomography (EIT) enables individualised PEEP titration by visualising regional lung collapse, facilitating lung-protective ventilation. However, evidence of its effect on clinical PPCs remains limited.

pubmed_facts.evidence: Abstract / unstructured: A human-centred partnership in the intensive care unit (ICU) aims to integrate person-centred care, communication, emotional support, equity, and collaboration into ICU environments. The European Society of Intensive Care Medicine (ESICM) developed a consensus statement on human-centred partnership in the ICU following a systematic, multi-phase, evidence-informed methodology incorporating the views of ICU professionals, academics, and patient and family representatives. This international multidisciplinary panel of 46 members conducted rapid reviews addressing 20 Population, Intervention, Comparator, Outcomes (PICO) questions across six domains: person-centred care; communication and transparency; emotional well-being; equity, diversity, and inclusion; ICU environment; technology and innovation. Based on the evidence synthesis, 53 draft statements were developed and evaluated through a two-round eDelphi study. The final set of statements was discussed and ratified at an expert consensus meeting with the initial panel of experts and with patients and family representatives. A total of 201 international stakeholders participated in round 1 and 149 in round 2. Members of the expert consensus meeting ultimately endorsed 43 consensus statements. Key recommendations supported flexible family visitation, structured interdisciplinary communication, empathy-based staff training, psychological support for patients and ICU professionals, culturally responsive care, environmental interventions to improve sleep and reduce delirium, and the integration of digital supported technologies. The consensus statement on human-centred partnership in the ICU provides a comprehensive framework for clinicians with evidence-informed directions to deliver high-quality practice across diverse ICU settings. By prioritising person-centred care, communication, inclusivity, and well-being alongside responsible technological innovation, the experiences and outcomes of patients, families, and ICU professionals may improve.

clinical_summary.text: In 395 patients undergoing total knee arthroplasty randomized to spinal or general anaesthesia, the anaesthesia method did not affect total operating room time. However, spinal anaesthesia was associated with longer postanaesthesia care unit stays but resulted in lower disposable material use and costs compared to general anaesthesia. These findings suggest resource and cost differences between anaesthesia types, though the choice did not impact operating room efficiency.

pubmed_facts.reported_results: Anaesthesia method did not affect operating room time (median 152 min [interquartile range 136-168 min] vs. 150 min [137-165 min], Hodges-Lehmann estimate 2 min [95% CI -3 to 6 min], p = 0.49). General anaesthesia generated more disposable material (1252 vs. 611 g), and both medicine and equipment expenses were higher (total costs €83 vs. €36).
pubmed_facts.conclusions:
With this anaesthesia regimen, knee arthroplasty patients occupied the operating room for a similar duration regardless of anaesthesia method, but patients required longer recovery in the postanaesthesia care unit after spinal anaesthesia. Regarding disposable material and medicine use, spinal anaesthesia appeared to be more economical and material-sparing than total intravenous anaesthesia. Furthermore, spinal anaesthesia appeared to cause less hypotension requiring haemodynamic interventions than general anaesthesia.
EDITORIAL COMMENT: This health-economic analysis estimates for how different aspects of general or spinal anaesthesia care contribute to process flow and item costs. Findings suggest that there may be measurably more costs associated with one of the anaesthesia type choices compared with the other, though this will depend on choices for materials and more.

Abstract / methods: A total of 395 patients undergoing total knee arthroplasty were randomised to spinal or general anaesthesia. Outcomes were total operating room time, non-operative operating room time, post-anaesthesia care unit time, use of drugs affecting haemodynamics, and the need for arterial cannulation and urinary catheterisation. In addition, we evaluated the financial costs and waste produced by single-use equipment and medicines in both anaesthesia methods.
Abstract / background: Spinal and general anaesthesia seem to lead to similar health-related outcomes in total knee arthroplasty. However, to produce economically and environmentally sustainable health care, we should also consider other factors. Current guidelines recommend preferring regional anaesthesia and total intravenous anaesthesia to reduce environmental impact. In this study, we analysed time, costs, and disposable materials associated with spinal anaesthesia and total intravenous anaesthesia during total knee arthroplasty.

Abstract / methods: Reviews of published literature were undertaken for commonly performed spinal procedures for pain, and the evidence was synthesised qualitatively. Evidence-based recommendations for each procedure were graded on a scale from A (strongest level) to D (not recommended), or as insufficient (I), using US Preventive Services Task Force criteria with the level of certainty rated as high, medium or low. All consensus recommendations required at least 75% agreement among the guideline panel. Good clinical practice statements were also developed.

pubmed.population_setting: In this prospective cohort study conducted at 2 tertiary hospitals in Athens, Greece, 102 hospitalized patients with COVID-19 pneumonia and 28 with non-COVID-19 community-acquired pneumonia were enrolled. On Day 1, release of TNFα and IL-6 was higher by the PBMCs of patients with COVID-19 pneumonia than non-COVID-19 CAP; the opposite was found for IL-1RA. Patients infected by the Omicron variant had higher production of TNFα and lower of IL-6. Using multivariate logistic regression analysis, it was confirmed that over-time decrease of the production of IL-6 by the PBMCs of patients with COVID-19 was a risk factor for progression into SRF and 28-day mortality.

Abstract / methods: In this prospective cohort study conducted at 2 tertiary hospitals in Athens, Greece, 102 hospitalized patients with COVID-19 pneumonia and 28 with non-COVID-19 community-acquired pneumonia were enrolled. Peripheral blood mononuclear cells were isolated during the first 24 hours before any immune intervention other than dexamethasone and stimulated for cytokine production. SRF was defined as a PaO₂/FiO₂ ratio <150 mmHg necessitating invasive or non-invasive ventilation. Exploratory serum microRNA sequencing was performed in a small subset.
Abstract / background: Dysregulated innate immunity contributes to COVID-19 severity, but its evolution over the periods of the pandemic is undefined. The aim of the study was to compare ex vivo innate immune responses in COVID-19 and non-COVID-19 community-acquired pneumonia (CAP) and assess associations with pandemic period, severe respiratory failure (SRF), mortality, and circulating microRNA patterns.

pubmed.population_setting: In this phase 3 open-label trial, we randomly assigned, in a 1:1:1 ratio, patients with muscle-invasive bladder cancer who were ineligible for or declined cisplatin-based chemotherapy to receive neoadjuvant durvalumab-enfortumab vedotin every 3 weeks for three cycles, followed by radical cystectomy and then adjuvant durvalumab every 4 weeks for nine cycles; neoadjuvant durvalumab-tremelimumab-enfortumab vedotin (tremelimumab for two cycles only), radical cystectomy, and adjuvant durvalumab-tremelimumab (tremelimumab for one cycle only); or radical cystectomy alone (control). In total, 233 patients were assigned to the durvalumab-enfortumab vedotin group, 233 to the durvalumab-tremelimumab-enfortumab vedotin group, and 229 to the control group. Grade 3 or higher adverse events occurred in 71.1% of patients in the durvalumab-enfortumab vedotin group (treatment-related, 30.7%), in 79.5% of those in the durvalumab-tremelimumab-enfortumab vedotin group (treatment-related, 44.5%), and in 50.2% of those in the control group.

Abstract / methods: In this multicenter observational cohort study, we included mechanically ventilated adult ICU survivors who underwent rehabilitation. Early sitting was defined as achievement of sitting at the bedside within 72 h after ICU admission. The primary outcome was death or functional decline at 3 months after hospital discharge, assessed using the Kihon Checklist. Prespecified secondary and exploratory outcomes included domain-specific impairments (physical, cognitive, and depressive), hospital readmission, and a composite of readmission or death within 3 months. Overlap propensity score weighting was used to balance baseline covariates. Multiple prespecified sensitivity analyses (48-h alternative definition, landmark analysis, exclusion of never-sitters, adjustment for Day-3 clinical status and rehabilitation dose) and Benjamini-Hochberg (BH) multiplicity adjustment were performed.

Perfusion index was lower, and reapplication rates were higher in ear group.

Abstract / methods: Pregnant women at ≥34 weeks gestation were randomized before delivery. Pulse oximetry probe was applied to either the right earlobe or right wrist immediately after birth using sensor-to-oximeter-first technique with Masimo® SET® rainbow® Radical-7® CO-Oximeter®. The primary outcome was time from completion of sensor application to reliable display of oxygen saturation and heart rate. Secondary outcomes included time from birth to start of sensor application, sensor application time, time from birth to reliable signal, perfusion index, and number of probe reapplications.
Abstract / objectives: Rapid acquisition of reliable pulse oximetry signals in delivery room is challenging due to transitional circulation, low peripheral perfusion, motion artifact, vernix, and skin edema. This randomized controlled trial compared right earlobe and right wrist pulse oximetry to determine differences in time to reliable signal acquisition.

clinical_summary.text: In adults undergoing pancreaticoduodenectomy with positive intraoperative bile cultures, withholding pre-emptive antibiotics did not increase early postoperative complications or infections compared to those who received antibiotics, based on a multicenter propensity-matched cohort study. However, five-year mortality was higher in the no-antibiotic group only in the matched cohort, a finding the authors caution may reflect residual confounding rather than a causal effect. These results suggest early outcomes are similar, but long-term survival implications remain uncertain.

Abstract / conclusions: A systematic difference between cRCTs and iRCTs in length-of-stay- or days-alive-type outcomes, but not mortality, was identified, with cRCTs reporting smaller effect size magnitudes than iRCTs. With under half of identified meta-analyses reporting on randomization modality, these results highlight the need for improved transparency and statistical consideration of randomization type in future meta-analyses in prehospital, emergency, and critical care.
Abstract / objectives: Cluster-randomized clinical trials (cRCTs) are pooled with individually randomized clinical trials (iRCTs) in meta-analyses. However, cRCTs are associated with methodological characteristics potentially inducing systematic differences compared with iRCTs. In acute settings, trial inclusion is time-sensitive, exacerbating inclusion-based biases. We conducted a meta-epidemiological study to assess deviations in effect estimates between cRCTs and iRCTs in these settings. DATA SOURCES: A systematic literature search was conducted in PubMed and Embase. DATA SELECTION: We screened and identified all meta-analyses in prehospital, emergency, or critical care within the last decade that included at least one cRCT and one iRCT. DATA EXTRACTION: Data were extracted in duplicate from the meta-analyses. If overlapping trials were identified, results were pooled. The primary outcome was mortality; the secondary outcome comprised length-of-stay- or days-alive-type outcomes. We identified 94 eligible meta-analyses; 44.7% reported on randomization type (cRCT or iRCT).

clinical_summary.text: In 395 patients undergoing total knee arthroplasty randomized to spinal or general anaesthesia, the anaesthesia method did not affect total operating room time. However, spinal anaesthesia was associated with longer postanaesthesia care unit stays but resulted in lower disposable material use and costs compared to general anaesthesia. These findings suggest resource and cost differences between anaesthesia types, though the choice did not impact operating room efficiency.
clinical_summary.result_quote: Anaesthesia method did not affect operating room time (median 152 min [interquartile range 136-168 min] vs. 150 min [137-165 min], Hodges-Lehmann estimate 2 min [95% CI -3 to 6 min], p = 0.49). However, after spinal anaesthesia, patients appeared to spend more time in the postanaesthesia care unit than after general anaesthesia (median 104 min [71-148 min] vs. 73 min [49-98 min], Hodges-Lehmann estimate 32 min [95% CI 23-42 min], p < 0.001).

Medication for hypotension was more common in the general anaesthesia group, whereas medication for hypertension was more common in the spinal anaesthesia group. General anaesthesia generated more disposable material (1252 vs. 611 g), and both medicine and equipment expenses were higher (total costs €83 vs. €36).

pubmed_facts.conclusions:
With this anaesthesia regimen, knee arthroplasty patients occupied the operating room for a similar duration regardless of anaesthesia method, but patients required longer recovery in the postanaesthesia care unit after spinal anaesthesia. Regarding disposable material and medicine use, spinal anaesthesia appeared to be more economical and material-sparing than total intravenous anaesthesia. Furthermore, spinal anaesthesia appeared to cause less hypotension requiring haemodynamic interventions than general anaesthesia.
EDITORIAL COMMENT: This health-economic analysis estimates for how different aspects of general or spinal anaesthesia care contribute to process flow and item costs. Findings suggest that there may be measurably more costs associated with one of the anaesthesia type choices compared with the other, though this will depend on choices for materials and more.

Abstract / methods: A total of 395 patients undergoing total knee arthroplasty were randomised to spinal or general anaesthesia. Outcomes were total operating room time, non-operative operating room time, post-anaesthesia care unit time, use of drugs affecting haemodynamics, and the need for arterial cannulation and urinary catheterisation. In addition, we evaluated the financial costs and waste produced by single-use equipment and medicines in both anaesthesia methods.
Abstract / background: Spinal and general anaesthesia seem to lead to similar health-related outcomes in total knee arthroplasty. However, to produce economically and environmentally sustainable health care, we should also consider other factors. Current guidelines recommend preferring regional anaesthesia and total intravenous anaesthesia to reduce environmental impact. In this study, we analysed time, costs, and disposable materials associated with spinal anaesthesia and total intravenous anaesthesia during total knee arthroplasty.

Abstract / methods: Pregnant women at ≥34 weeks gestation were randomized before delivery. Pulse oximetry probe was applied to either the right earlobe or right wrist immediately after birth using sensor-to-oximeter-first technique with Masimo® SET® rainbow® Radical-7® CO-Oximeter®. The primary outcome was time from completion of sensor application to reliable display of oxygen saturation and heart rate. Secondary outcomes included time from birth to start of sensor application, sensor application time, time from birth to reliable signal, perfusion index, and number of probe reapplications.
Abstract / objectives: Rapid acquisition of reliable pulse oximetry signals in delivery room is challenging due to transitional circulation, low peripheral perfusion, motion artifact, vernix, and skin edema. This randomized controlled trial compared right earlobe and right wrist pulse oximetry to determine differences in time to reliable signal acquisition.

pubmed.population_setting: We performed a systematic review and Bayesian random-effects meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials (RCTs) comparing intravenous sodium bicarbonate with placebo or usual care in adult intensive care unit patients with metabolic acidosis. Four RCTs including 1544 patients were analysed.

clinical_context.uncertainty: No statistically significant benefit demonstrated; no-effect/equivalence not established

clinical_summary.text: In critically ill adults with metabolic acidosis, intravenous sodium bicarbonate therapy compared to placebo or usual care did not demonstrate a clear short-term mortality benefit in a Bayesian meta-analysis of four randomized trials. However, sodium bicarbonate was associated with a lower risk of renal replacement therapy (RRT) initiation, though effects on other outcomes were small or uncertain. The practical implication is that while survival benefit remains unproven, sodium bicarbonate may reduce the need for RRT in this population.
clinical_summary.result_quote: Sodium bicarbonate did not show a clear short-term mortality benefit (RR 0.94, 95% CrI 0.73-1.22), with a posterior probability of benefit of 72.1%.

pubmed_facts.reported_results: Four RCTs including 1544 patients were analysed. Sodium bicarbonate did not show a clear short-term mortality benefit (RR 0.94, 95% CrI 0.73-1.22), with a posterior probability of benefit of 72.1%. For RRT initiation, sodium bicarbonate was associated with a lower risk (RR 0.74, 95% CrI 0.59-0.98), with a posterior probability of benefit of 97.2%. Effects on other outcomes were small or imprecise, and no consistent safety signal was identified.

pubmed_facts.conclusions: Current randomised evidence does not demonstrate a clear survival benefit from sodium bicarbonate therapy in critically ill adults with metabolic acidosis, but suggests a high probability of reducing RRT initiation. Abstract / methods: We performed a systematic review and Bayesian random-effects meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials (RCTs) comparing intravenous sodium bicarbonate with placebo or usual care in adult intensive care unit patients with metabolic acidosis. MEDLINE, Embase and CENTRAL were searched from inception to December 2025, with an updated search on 2 April 2026. The primary outcome was short-term all-cause mortality. - Key results: Sodium bicarbonate did not show a clear short-term mortality benefit (RR 0.94, 95% CrI 0.73-1.22), with a posterior probability of benefit of 72.1%.
- Secondary results (do not replace the primary outcome): Four RCTs including 1544 patients were analysed. For RRT initiation, sodium bicarbonate was associated with a lower risk (RR 0.74, 95% CrI 0.59-0.98), with a posterior probability of benefit of 97.2%. Effects on other outcomes were small or imprecise, and no consistent safety signal was identified.

- Not explicitly reported in the supplied evidence.
- Source basis: abstract_and_fulltext_excerpt

pubmed_facts.reported_results:
Between May 1, 2019 and Jan 13, 2026, 1045 patients were eligible for enrolment. The trial was stopped early for futility and slow enrolment after 424 of 600 planned patients were recruited. 126 patients were randomly assigned to the supine and conventional mechanical ventilation group, 130 to the prone and conventional mechanical ventilation group, 90 to the supine and HFOV group, and 78 to the prone and HFOV group. Median age was 3·3 years (IQR 1·1-10·1), 211 (50%) patients were female, and 213 (50%) were male. There were no significant differences in ventilator-free days between prone and supine positioning (median 17·9 days [IQR 8·9-21·3] vs 17·4 days [6·4-21·9]; Hodges-Lehmann location shift adjusting for ventilation 0·0 [95% CI -0·8 to 1·0]) or between HFOV and conventional mechanical ventilation (17·3 [5·7-21·6] vs 18·0 [9·9-21·5]; Hodges-Lehmann location shift adjusting for positioning -0·3 [95% CI -1·5 to 0·5]). 41 (10%) patients had died at day 28, without group differences. Plugging or obstruction of the artificial airway occurred more frequently with prone than supine positioning (14 events in 12 [6%] of 188 patients vs three events in three [2%] of 197 patients; 0·74 [95% CI 0·44-1·26] vs 0·15 [0·05-0·47] events per 100 artificial airway days; rate ratio 4·83 [95% CI 1·38-16·82]). Stage 2 or worse immobility-related pressure injuries also occurred more frequently with prone versus supine positioning (12 [6%] vs two [1%]; relative risk 6·13 [95% CI 1·45-25·97]). Haemodynamic instability occurred more frequently with HFOV than conventional mechanical ventilation (41 events in 19 [13%] of 141 patients vs 38 events in 22 [9%] of 244 patients; 2·21 [95% CI 1·63-3·00] vs 1·22 [0·89-1·68] events per 100 paediatric intensive care unit days; rate ratio 1·84 [95% CI 1·18-2·87]). One serious adverse event, an unwitnessed self-extubation followed by cardiopulmonary arrest, occurred in a patient in the prone and conventional mechanical ventilation group.
INTERPRETATION: We found no evidence to support prone positioning or HFOV as first-line strategies to improve ventilator-free days in patients with early, moderate-to-severe PARDS. Thus, the routine use of these strategies in this population is not recommended.
FUNDING: US National Institutes of Health/National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute.

Abstract / methods: PROSpect was an international, two-by-two factorial, response-adaptive, phase 3, randomised controlled trial done in 75 paediatric intensive care units in 18 countries. Eligible patients were aged 2 weeks to 20 years, and were intubated and mechanically ventilated for less than 96 h before meeting criteria for moderate-to-severe PARDS. Patients were centrally randomly assigned using a web-based system to supine positioning and conventional mechanical ventilation, prone positioning and conventional mechanical ventilation, supine positioning and HFOV, or prone positioning and HFOV. Initially, the allocation was 1:1:1:1 stratified by age group and direct or indirect lung injury using a permuted block design with blocks of four and eight. Response-adaptive randomisation updates were planned to adjust allocation probabilities 28 days after 300 patients were randomly assigned and then 28 days after every 100 additional patients. Given the nature of the interventions, masking was not possible. The primary outcome was ventilator-free days through to day 28 among all randomly assigned participants. This study was registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT03896763) and is closed to enrolment.
Abstract / background: Data on prone positioning and high-frequency oscillatory ventilation (HFOV) used separately or in combination in patients with paediatric acute respiratory distress syndrome (PARDS) are inconclusive, leading to wide practice variability. We aimed to compare the effects of prone positioning with supine positioning and the effects of HFOV with conventional mechanical ventilation on ventilator-free days in children with early, moderate-to-severe PARDS.

pubmed_facts.intervention_comparator: Prospective, Before/After quality assurance study determining adherence to AHA ventilation guidelines in adults with out-of-hospital cardiac arrest treated by Milwaukee County Emergency Medical Services and Kenosha Fire in Wisconsin using (Before) end tidal carbon dioxide [ETCO2] to monitor ventilations - Real BVM Help® applied but blinded versus (After) Real BVM Help®.
pubmed_facts.primary_endpoint: mean per-person proportion (%) of ventilations in-target for rate, tidal volume, and both rate and tidal volume. AHA 2020 guidelines were followed.
pubmed_facts.reported_results: From 9/29/22-12/22/23, 278 patients were entered (148 Before/130 After). Average age: 62.3±16.7 years; 185 (67%) male. Mean per-person proportion (%) of ventilations in Before/After Groups in-target for rate (47.7±25.1% vs 74.4±24.1% respectively, p<0.0001), tidal volume (15.3±15.4% vs 45.4±23.8% respectively, p<0.0001), and rate and tidal volume (7.5±9.6% vs 39.0±23.3% respectively, p<0.0001) were significantly higher in the After Group. In the Before Group, using ETCO2 to monitor all ventilations (N=22,037 ventilations), only 43.8% were in-target for rate, 13.5% in-target for tidal volume, and 6.8% in-target for rate and tidal volume with a lower-than-target tidal volume delivered in 58.2% of all ventilations.

pubmed_facts.conclusions: Real BVM Help® was associated with statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvement in adherence to AHA ventilation guidelines. pubmed_facts.primary_endpoint: Primary outcome is the sensitivity for cardiac arrest detection.
pubmed_facts.reported_results:
From 6,344 records screened, 13 publications were included with the number of participants ranging from 18 to 1,423. Wristbands were the most prevalent device type (n=9). Nine studies used photoplethysmography as primary sensor type, with accelerometry as additive sensor modality (n=2). Other sensors used were mechanical plethysmography (n=1), electrocardiography (n=1), sound-based (n=1) and a nonlinear resonant circuit (n=1). Sensitivity ranged between 43.8 and 100%, with ten studies reporting a sensitivity of ≥ 90%. False positives ranged between multiple per day and one per twenty-one user-years.
DISCUSSION: Wearable devices have demonstrated promising sensitivity for detecting cardiac arrest. However, (external) validation and real-life data are scarce, and the sensitivity-false alarm trade-off requires further investigation.
REGISTRATION: OSF, doi: https://doi.org/10.17605/OSF.IO/AEPF8.

Abstract / methods: A systematic search was performed using PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, Embase, the Cochrane Libraries, forward citation and backward citation to identify all eligible studies up to 22 September 2026. Studies describing non-invasive, intended wearable systems designed to detect OHCA and reporting on their detection performance were included. The methodology and report of the present review are based on recommendations of the PRISMA statement and Cochrane Collaboration. Primary outcome is the sensitivity for cardiac arrest detection. Secondary outcomes include false positives cardiac arrest alerts and specificity. Studies were evaluated using the QUADAS-2 tool.

pubmed_facts.reported_results:
Our systematic review identified five randomised trials, all of which provided individual participant data. Among these, the definition of the primary safety outcome varied, and in four trials emergency department length of stay was not reported for the whole analysis population. We included 110 933 patient presentations (55 489 managed with the 0/1 h pathway and 55 444 managed with the 0/3 h pathway). Within 30 days, all-cause death or new type 1 myocardial infarction occurred in 446 patient presentations (0·8%) with the 0/1 h pathway versus 562 patient presentations (1·0%) with the 0/3 h pathway (random-effects pooled odds ratio [OR] 0·83 [95% CI 0·45-1·53]; I2=62·9%; τ2=0·143). Emergency department length of stay was 314 min (IQR 211-481) in the 0/1 h pathway group versus 308 min (209-453) in the 0/3 h pathway group (random-effects pooled geometric mean ratio 1·03 [95% CI 0·85-1·25]; I2=99·2%; τ2=0·024). Direct discharge from the emergency department occurred in 37 190 patient presentations (67·0%) with the 0/1 h pathway versus 36 485 patient presentations (65·8%) with the 0/3 h pathway (random-effects pooled OR 1·31 [95% CI 0·79-2·16]; I2=97·8%; τ2=0·156).
INTERPRETATION: Across the available randomised trials, short-term adverse event rates were low with both pathways, but the pooled safety estimate remained imprecise. On average, earlier cardiac troponin retesting did not reduce emergency department length of stay or clearly increase direct discharge, and substantial between-study heterogeneity indicates that treatment effects might not translate uniformly across health-care systems. For hospitals considering transitioning from a 0/3 h to a 0/1 h pathway, implementation decisions should take broader diagnostic and organisational considerations into account.
FUNDING: Swiss National Science Foundation, Swiss Heart Foundation, University Hospital Basel, University of Basel, and Foundation for Cardiovascular Research Basel.

Abstract / methods: In this systematic review and individual participant data meta-analysis, we searched PubMed, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, Scopus, and the International Clinical Trials Registry Platform from inception to July 6, 2026, without language restrictions, for randomised trials comparing the safety and efficacy of 0/1 h versus 0/3 h pathways (blood draws at 0 h and 3 h, ie, standard care). Individual participant data were obtained and outcome definitions were harmonised. The primary analysis used a two-stage random-effects meta-analysis. After receipt of the individual participant data but before data harmonisation or analysis, the primary safety outcome was refined to a composite of all-cause death or new type 1 myocardial infarction within 30 days, from the originally specified composite of all-cause death or any new myocardial infarction. The primary efficacy outcomes were emergency department length of stay and direct discharge from the emergency department. This meta-analysis is registered with PROSPERO (CRD420261383452).
Abstract / background: In patients with suspected myocardial infarction, the 0/1 h pathway (blood draws at 0 h and 1 h) is recommended in current guidelines for early risk stratification. However, individual trials used different safety outcomes, and efficacy outcomes were inconclusive or not assessed. We conducted a systematic review and individual participant data meta-analysis of all randomised controlled trials to synthesise the totality of the evidence, assess heterogeneity across trials, and evaluate clinically relevant outcomes using harmonised definitions across trials.

pubmed_facts.primary_endpoint: The primary outcome was six-month all-cause mortality, and the secondary outcome was poor functional outcome (modified Rankin scale score 4-6).
pubmed_facts.reported_results: All 2789 adult OHCA patients from the trials' primary analyses were included (median age 65 years (IQR 56-73), 79.9% male). Death occurred in 49.4% of patients in the 33 °C group, and in 47.9% in the controlled normothermia group. Variation in six-month mortality ITEs estimated from ischemic burden correlates and initial neurological findings was minimal, and no significant heterogeneity of treatment effect was identified across all methods and analysis populations. In the pooled analysis, estimated conditional mean mortality risk difference ranged from - 1.2% to 2.1% in causal forest (p = 0.99), and from - 0.5% to 1.5% in BART, with posterior probabilities for hypothermia benefit ranging from 42% to 53%. Absolute subgroup estimates in TEM-VIP analysis were small and non-significant. Results were consistent for the six-month functional outcome.

pubmed_facts.evidence: Abstract / unstructured: Pharmacotherapy remains an important component of multidisciplinary, multimodal pain treatment. Based on a well-established understanding of multiple concurrent mechanisms of nociceptive transmission and modulation, the demonstrated potential for synergistic interactions of drug combinations seen in preclinical studies supports the hypothesis of superior analgesia, and possibly also, fewer side-effects as compared with monotherapy. Likely related to this hypothesis and rationale, real-world evidence shows that approximately half of all patients with chronic pain, and even more with acute pain, concurrently receive 2 or more drugs from different mechanistic classes. To date, many dozens of randomized controlled trials have evaluated various analgesic combinations for the treatment of postoperative, neuropathic, back, arthritis, fibromyalgia, pelvic, and cancer-related pain conditions. Despite this growing area of research, most analgesic drug combinations are currently administered without rigorous evidence, thus exposing patients to the added cost or risk of some combinations that are not necessarily superior to monotherapy. As such, we propose future efforts to more efficiently exploit the potential benefits of combination therapy including: (1) expansion and coordination of translational collaborations to prioritize the most beneficial and clinically relevant combinations; (2) ensuring that preclinical combination studies evaluate multiple drug dosages and multiple relevant adverse effects; (3) ensuring that clinical trials include comparisons with each and every monotherapy component of the combination; (4) conducting further real-world studies of clinically beneficial combinations to ensure safety and efficacy in broader clinical settings; and (5) the application of these principles also to the evaluation of nonpharmacological treatment combinations.

pubmed_facts.reported_results:
We included 33 studies involving 580,197 patients. Twenty-nine studies (579,737 patients) reported pulmonary aspiration. The pooled incidence of pulmonary aspiration was 0.03% (95%CI 0.01-0.09%) with conventional fasting policies and 0.03% (95%CI 0.01-0.09%) with liberal policies. Risk ratios were available from 14 studies (475,399 patients) and showed no difference in pulmonary aspiration between policies (risk ratio 0.77, 95%CI 0.40-1.47). Seventeen studies (344,653 patients) reported vomiting; the pooled incidence was 0.99% (95%CI 0.27-3.51%) with conventional policies and 0.76% (95%CI 0.18-3.14%) with liberal policies. The certainty of evidence was very low for both outcomes.
DISCUSSION: Pulmonary aspiration is rare in children, and similar incidences of aspiration and vomiting were observed under liberal and conventional clear fluid fasting policies. The results should be interpreted cautiously due to the very low certainty of evidence.
